openObligations: The complete actual published article pages 1229-1232 and complete PMC author main text were read. The published version has three figures, whereas the longer author manuscript has five; locators retain both mappings. The published PDF also contains portions of unrelated adjacent articles, which supply no evidence here.

The Supporting Online Material was not read: direct archive endpoints returned small HTML challenges and publisher access failed. Complete RNA preparation, calibration, background/no-enzyme controls, replicate definitions and supplementary figures S1-S2 are not reconstructed. Main-text assay details and its observed finite transfer series are the admitted boundary.

The catalysts are RNA ligases supplied as a starting seed and assembled from supplied sequence-specific oligoribonucleotide fragments with activated 5-prime triphosphates. This is not nucleotide-by-nucleotide copying, arbitrary genome replication, de novo nucleotide/fragment synthesis, or self-production of every resource.

The pair assay contains no proteins during amplification. Prior laboratory synthesis/evolution/preparation can use biological machinery; absence of proteins in the amplification vessel does not mean the entire experimental production history was protein-free.

A denaturing gel separates labeled substrates and full-length ligation products; the source fits product accumulation to a logistic growth model. That fit and the reciprocal reaction topology support finite cross-catalytic amplification, not an independently reconstructed fold/tertiary structure or proof of every catalytic-closure axiom of an arbitrary RAF network.

Single-batch growth levels off as substrates are depleted. Six successive five-hour incubations with 4 percent carryover and fresh substrate demonstrate 30 hours of operation; the reported cumulative amplification greater than 10^8 accounts for serial dilution and is not the final vessel concentration. Indefinite continuation is conditional extrapolation beyond the observed series.

The mixed population is a different preparation with 15 mM rather than 25 mM MgCl2, many supplied substrates and 5 percent transfer. Its finite 100-hour result is read but not a second independent publication or the same paired-assay context. It is not admitted here as open-ended evolution or a new arbitrary-function genetic system.

No protein-folding prerequisite, universal protein catalytic ancestry, site cooperativity, allosteric feedback, physical compartment requirement, spontaneous prebiotic origin, unrestricted food generation, living autonomy or universal network persistence is established.
No raw gel acquisition, independent fit, isotope/radiolabel calibration, numerical replay, experimental replication or new experimental optimization was performed.

records.description: Biochemical or enzymatic modulation of a specified electron-capture channel remains an unsupported hypothesis within this review. The existing isotope-specific Pr140 storage-ring result establishes an electronic-state dependence in highly stripped ions; it does not establish the asserted biochemical intervention. The draft empirical extension is excluded from the admitted findings without claiming that all biochemical electron-capture effects are absent.
records.name: Biochemical electron-capture modulation: unsupported hypothesis
openObligations: The existing reviewed positive case concerns highly ionized stored 140Pr charge states in a high-vacuum storage ring, not biochemical coordination, enzymes, cells or a matched chemical intervention. Its Schottky populations, loss-corrected partial rates and conditional hyperfine explanation cannot serve as positive evidence for this biochemical extension.
The asserted chemical/enzymatic experimental support is excluded from this admission; the broader biochemical dependence remains explicitly unsupported here.

This is a statement about what the present review has admitted. No comprehensive search of chemical or biochemical electron-capture literature has been performed, and no absence of such effects throughout the literature or in nature is asserted.

Electronic occupancy, electron density at the nucleus, nuclear/electronic angular momentum and state populations are distinct dependencies. The selected Pr140 H-like/He-like contrast does not supply a universal electron-density coefficient or monotonic electron-count law. A biochemical binding-context mechanism would require its own specified channel and comparison.

The source does not demonstrate altered underlying nuclear forces or an enzyme-catalyzed nuclear reaction. Ionization preserves which parent isotope is prepared; the subsequent EC transition changes the nuclear charge and element.

A stronger admission would need an identified isotope and EC channel, a specified biochemical/electronic preparation and matched control, a channel-specific rate observable with background/loss separation, and stated inference uncertainties. Those are open obligations rather than results of the current ion experiment.

openObligations: The source defines kobs as the approach-to-equilibrium rate, kcleave+kligate. It reflects the rapidly reacting population and is not kcat, isolated chemical cleavage or a folding rate.

The total cleaved fraction plateaus differ by ion and preparation. In 0.1 M NaCl source plateaus 0.36-0.69 include inactive/slowly reacting fractions, so amplitude is not simply the internal cleavage/ligation equilibrium constant.

Mn230±25 min^-1 in 2 M NaCl at 1 mM Mn, pH 7 is a source-calculated extrapolation from a measured 3.5 min^-1 at 0.15 mM Mn, pH 6, assuming linear metal and log-linear pH dependence. It is not a directly measured high-salt 230 min^-1 trace.

Unresolved source conflict: the visually read Table 1 image prints a high-salt Ca upper entry<=0.50 min^-1, while the prose/abstract state>4600-fold Mn/Ca separation using the 230 min^-1 extrapolation. Those displayed entries alone do not establish that quoted bound. Preserve both without silently replacing 0.50 by 0.05 or inventing a corrected ratio.

Table 1 nominal values are averages of at least three experiments with one-standard-deviation errors, not fitted covariance or independent laboratories. Gel quantification, quench-flow response and metal-property regressions were not replayed.

Metal stocks were checked by ICP optical emission and buffers treated with Chelex/EDTA; actual free-ion activities were not newly calibrated here. Nominal added-metal concentration is not a directly measured catalytic-site occupancy.
Monovalent-only600 mM Na or NH4 assays give source upper limitskobs<0.02 min^-1, not a universal zero activity or proof of obligatory divalent-metal chemistry for all ribozymes.

Main-text reports of pulse-chase and native-gel controls constrain substrate exchange as an alternative to slow activation. The underlying Supplemental Figure S2 was not directly reviewed; a single native-gel band does not exclude unresolved local conformations.

Dilute to about 25 nM in 50 mM Tris, pH 7.0, 100 mM NaCl and 0.1 mM EDTA; at 25 C titrate Ca, Mg, Mn, Sr or specified monovalent ions. records.name: Prepared hammerhead I-II FRET and ion controls
openObligations: Boots FRET uses chemically synthesized Cy3/Cy5-labelled complexes with a deoxy cleavage-site substrate, at about 25 nM complex. Main cleavage kinetics use mostly T7-transcribed cleavable RNA at 0.5-1 micromolar ribozyme with a 10:1 strand ratio. They are linked but distinct preparations, not simultaneous structure and chemistry of one molecule.

The I-II dye pair reports global stem proximity. The source explicitly says it cannot establish formation of the specific loop-loop tertiary contact or a unique catalytically active local conformation.

Source two-state/Hill assumptions may not hold microscopically; fitted midpoints compare empirical global-folding responses rather than determine metal-binding mechanisms, microscopicKD or bound-ion counts. n less than 1 is not a fractional ion molecule count.

The labelled construct was selected because its fast-population kobs agreed with unlabelled RNA, reported as data not shown. Chemically synthesized and transcribed strands nevertheless have different cleavage plateaus, so equality of the fast rate does not validate equality of active fractions.

Replacing loop II with UUCG changes the donor position as well as possible tertiary interaction. Different FRET amplitudes cannot alone quantify the same distance or population change across these variants.
The four-ion FRET comparison covers Ca, Mg, Mn and Sr. Co, Zn and Cd are excluded because of optical interference or solubility; no absent FRET result is filled in from the kinetic series.

Source dye-only controls showed Mn quenching above 10 mM; the source applied a linear correction, about 10% at 60 mM. Raw spectra/corrections were not independently replayed. High-salt and high-ion conditions are in vitro regimes rather than whole-cell measurements.

Table 2 values are source averages of three or more experiments with one-standard-deviation errors. These sampling summaries are not full fit covariance, microscopic binding constants or independently reproduced confidence intervals.

limitations: The admitted primary acquisition is 8.3 mM bovine pancreatic trypsin inhibitor at pH* 5.2 in isotope-enriched aqueous emulsion droplets at -10 and -30 C. pH* is uncorrected for isotope effects. This is not a physiological-temperature cellular solution or an ionic-shell experiment.

Lorentzian amplitudes/correlation times, water-class assignments and rotational retardation are source-model inferences. The fixed hydration number 268 is estimated from existing 5PTI solvent-accessible area, 1.4 angstrom probe and 15 square-angstrom area per water; it is not a direct counted population.

The reported beta amplitudes are apparent Nbeta*Sbeta^2 products affected by exchange and orientational order. They are not integer water counts, unique hydration-site occupancies or directly measured residence times.

The highest-frequency point is excluded from the source mono-Lorentzian fits. A weak second component is suggested; its amplitude and the frequency-independent term have large covariance. Missing raw data and full covariance prevent an independent fit or unique distribution reconstruction.

Protein rotational times 14/70 ns at -10/-30 C are viscosity/isotope/hydrodynamic-scaled adopted estimates from earlier relaxation, not new direct measurements of tumbling in these samples. Surface/internal separation depends on these and exchange assumptions.

SI S7 notes that the expected W111 internal-water behavior at -30 C is inconsistent with the observed dispersion. A local structural transformation causing much slower exchange is proposed but not measured; complete external-surface attribution remains conditional.

The source infers modest mobility retardation for most surface-contact waters, not static long-range ordering, an immobilized shell, a universal no-more-than-two bound at all temperatures, or the same timescale at every residue.

Converting rotational relaxation into residence/translational times requires additional assumptions. The source 24 ps estimate at 4 C and room-temperature extrapolations are not direct primary observations at those temperatures and are not admitted as new measurements.

No ion positions, ion number/density, electrostatic potential, hydrogen-bond energy, dielectric shell, catalysis, recognition change, binding thermodynamics or protein-stability perturbation is measured by the selected acquisition.

Long-range dipolar contributions to an NOE measurement describe nonlocal magnetic sampling. They do not establish long-range structural ordering of water or ions. The paper new oxytocin and older BPTI NOE analyses are read but supply no additional admitted acquisition context or independent replication here.

The emulsion-interface control, BPTI self-association estimates, internal-water coordinates and stability/cold-denaturation arguments include earlier-work inputs. No universal absence of aggregation/interface effects or direct new folding/structure determination is inferred.
